output.summary: The run is VALID, but the capacity analysis is INDETERMINATE and the policy verdict is NO_POLICY. Both stage windows (step-1 ~100 users, step-2 ~200 users) had complete resource bins, passing diagnostic generator-CPU guards, and NO_POLICY window summaries because no business policy rule and no resource rule with effect: sla was applicable (CAPACITY_SLA_MISSING). Because no stage had an applicable SLA, no stage outcome was verified (CAPACITY_STAGE_NOT_VERIFIED), so no capacity bound was produced (lower_inclusive null, upper_exclusive null) and the observed achieved values 97 and 197 are not product-verified bounds. capacity_knee is null only because KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED is a fixed product limitation, separate from the missing-SLA cause. To obtain PASS/FAIL and a bound, configure an applicable SLA rule for each stage and rerun. Keep NO_POLICY distinct from PASS, verify clocks before any temporal interpretation, and do not treat zero recorded errors, empty findings, or complete bins as proof of stability or spare capacity.

hypotheses.observation: Window policy summaries for stage-1 and stage-2 both report verdict NO_POLICY for business and resource verdicts, the overall policy_verdict is NO_POLICY, and the capacity summary lists reason CAPACITY_SLA_MISSING.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The product found no applicable rule to evaluate in those windows: no business policy rule and no resource rule with effect: sla. NO_POLICY means no rule was evaluated, not that the stage passed; healthy-looking numbers do not turn it into PASS.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the policy set and the test definition to confirm whether an SLA rule (business policy rule or resource rule with effect: sla) is configured to cover each stage window; if not, configure one for the missing scope and rerun.

hypotheses.observation: The capacity summary has bound_type INDETERMINATE with lower_inclusive and upper_exclusive null; each stage has verdict NO_POLICY and verified_bound_load null, and capacity reasons include CAPACITY_SLA_MISSING and CAPACITY_STAGE_NOT_VERIFIED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Because no stage had an applicable SLA, the product could not verify a product outcome for any stage, so no capacity bound could be derived from verified stages; the achieved p05 values (97 and 197) are observed load statistics, not product-verified bounds.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Add an applicable SLA rule for each stage and rerun, then confirm each stage has a verified product outcome and that a bounded capacity value is reported by the capacity summary.

hypotheses.observation: capacity_knee is null with knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, while the bound-relevant reasons are CAPACITY_SLA_MISSING and CAPACITY_STAGE_NOT_VERIFIED.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The knee detector is a fixed, not-implemented product capability, so capacity_knee is always null in this product version; it is not a defect of this run and is not the cause of the indeterminate bound, which is explained by the missing SLA and unverified stages.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Do not try to implement or enable a knee detector. Focus on configuring an applicable SLA for each stage so stages can be verified; on rerun expect capacity_knee to remain null.

hypotheses.observation: The diagnostic generator-cpu-guard (rule_id generator-cpu-guard, effect diagnostic, threshold 0.85, operator gt) reports status PASS for both stage-1 and stage-2, and generator CPU series are in the 0.41 to 0.45 ratio range with 30/30 cells present.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The generator guard is diagnostic by contract: its PASS indicates the guard condition held but it does not create an upper capacity bound and cannot convert NO_POLICY into PASS. Generator health is therefore not the reason the bound is indeterminate.
hypotheses.recommended_check: If generator health must be investigated further, inspect the generator resource series (active_users, cpu_used) directly; a rerun with a healthy generator is an acceptable check but will not change NO_POLICY unless an SLA rule is configured.

hypotheses.observation: The resource binding reports clock_alignment 'not_verified_by_core' for the explicit windows used to evaluate the run.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Because the core did not verify clock alignment between the sources contributing to the result and resource series, any lead/lag ordering or time-based causal claim derived from these series is unsupported.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Verify clock synchronization/alignment across telemetry sources before interpreting any temporal relationship between the result and resource series.

hypotheses.observation: Overall and checkout metric summaries report max latency 1500 ms while p95 is 140 ms and p99 is 140 ms, with error_count 0 over 2401 samples.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The max latency is an apparent outlier relative to the reported p99; a small number of samples may have experienced elevated latency, but the referenced summaries do not give per-bin timing or event context, so no cause or impact can be attributed.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Inspect the per-bin latency series and the surrounding samples around the maximum to determine whether the outlier is isolated before drawing any conclusion.

recommendations.action: Configure an applicable SLA rule (a business policy rule or a resource rule with effect: sla) covering each stage window, then rerun.
recommendations.rationale: The window summaries and capacity summary are NO_POLICY because CAPACITY_SLA_MISSING; the product only yields PASS/FAIL and a capacity bound when such a rule exists for the window.

recommendations.action: After configuring the SLA, rerun and confirm stage outcomes are verified and that a bounded capacity value is reported; keep the observed achieved values (97 and 197) distinct from product-verified bounds.
recommendations.rationale: Currently verified_bound_load is null and the bound is INDETERMINATE with CAPACITY_STAGE_NOT_VERIFIED; a capacity bound can only be derived from stages with a verified product outcome.

recommendations.action: Before any temporal interpretation, verify clock alignment across telemetry sources.
recommendations.rationale: The resource binding reports clock_alignment not_verified_by_core, so lead/lag ordering or temporal causal hypotheses are unsupported until clocks are verified.

recommendations.action: Inspect per-bin latency and throughput data around the 1500 ms maximum latency sample.
recommendations.rationale: p99 latency is 140 ms and error_count is 0, so the maximum may be an isolated outlier; only per-bin evidence can support how many samples were affected.

recommendations.action: Do not treat NO_POLICY, empty findings, or zero recorded errors as evidence of stability or spare capacity; treat the capacity verdict as indeterminate.
recommendations.rationale: The product reports NO_POLICY when no applicable rule exists, findings is empty, and run-scope counts are not policy-window denominators; absence of recorded findings does not prove absence of a problem.

recommendations.action: If generator health needs further assurance, inspect the active_users and cpu_used generator series and rerun with a healthy generator; leave the generator guard's diagnostic effect unchanged.
recommendations.rationale: The generator-cpu-guard is diagnostic by contract; it passed, but a passing diagnostic guard does not create a capacity bound or change NO_POLICY.

caveats: NO_POLICY is not PASS: the product reports NO_POLICY because no business policy rule and no resource rule with effect: sla applied to the windows; a healthy-looking window or a rerun does not turn it into PASS.

The capacity bound is INDETERMINATE (lower_inclusive null, upper_exclusive null) with analysis_coverage INCOMPLETE (CAPACITY_SLA_MISSING, CAPACITY_STAGE_NOT_VERIFIED); no capacity conclusion can be drawn from this run.

The achieved values 97 and 197 (p05_10s, load axis users) are observed load statistics for the target loads of 100 and 200; they are not product-verified capacity bounds because stage verdicts are NO_POLICY and verified_bound_load is null.
capacity_knee is null because KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED is a fixed product limitation, not a defect of this run and not something a test operator can enable or fix.
clock_alignment is not_verified_by_core for the resource binding; timing-based ordering or causal claims are unsupported until clocks are verified.
The generator CPU guard is diagnostic by contract (effect diagnostic); its PASS does not create an upper bound and its effect should not be changed to binding, SLA, or enforcing.

Overall-run totals (sample_count 2401, error_rate 0/2401) are run-scope quantities and differ from policy-window denominators; zero recorded errors and absent findings do not prove stability, spare capacity, or the absence of a problem.
run_validity VALID refers to run mechanics and does not imply that policies were complete or applicable.
